mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate predicts higher discount rates for future cash flows, reducing the present value of expected equity returns and thus driving negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) coinciding with UNRATE below 4% signals a tight labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases over next month
failure_condition: In 60-day rolling window, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically positive when trigger condition is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GDPC1 (real GDP) over the prior quarter suggests stronger economic demand, which lowers the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the mean of prior 60-day windows (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below trend indicates weakening supply-side momentum, which raises uncertainty and compresses future earnings expectations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive 20-day windows, 20-day returns are not consistently negative (average p-value > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, the higher policy rate increases the real discount rate, depressing expected equity returns and causing negative 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 10 such trigger events, 5-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3% followed by a rise in HOUST (housing starts) indicates a labor market recovery accelerating housing demand, which supports equity valuations and yields positive 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3% and HOUST increases over next 2 months
regime_hint: labor market softening turning to recovery
failure_condition: In 30 instances of this trigger, 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in RSAFS (retail sales) suggest weakening consumer demand, raising uncertainty and lowering growth expectations, which results in negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 6 months, 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (average p-value > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% for three consecutive months reduces the real risk premium, lowering discount rates and producing positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During 10 such inflation periods, 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
